title: Zoo Planet
intro: Zoo Planet runs in three regions with a dozen services. The arrows are what the system does today. Drag each pattern block onto the place where it belongs, then link it to the components it must talk to. Two places are traps.

blocks.label: Singleflight and hash ring
blocks.blurb: One model call per hot key, stale answers while it refreshes, keys that stay put.

blocks.label: Global GCRA limiter
blocks.blurb: One smooth budget per caller across every region, on the store's clock.

blocks.label: Hedging and admission
blocks.blurb: Backup requests for the slow tail, a concurrency cap and priority shedding.

blocks.label: Outbox relay and inbox
blocks.blurb: Events committed with the order, published later, applied once.

blocks.label: Propagation and tail sampler
blocks.blurb: One trace across the queue, kept or dropped once it is complete.

blocks.label: Shard router and rebalancer
blocks.blurb: A ring of virtual nodes, an online migration and a k-way merge.

blocks.label: Saga orchestrator
blocks.blurb: Steps, retries and compensations, with a durable log to resume from.

blocks.label: Partitioned log
blocks.blurb: Keyed partitions, a consumer group that rebalances, commits after work.

blocks.label: Geospatial index
blocks.blurb: Cells around the visitor instead of every keeper in the city.

blocks.label: Leases and fencing
blocks.blurb: One leader at a time, and a ledger that rejects the old one.

01.hint: It decides which node owns a question and who is allowed to recompute it.

02.hint: Every region must agree on one number, and only one component is shared by all of them.

03.hint: It chooses which replica serves a call, and when to ask a second one.

04.hint: The event must be born in the same transaction as the order, and the receiving side must remember what it applied.

05.hint: It sees the spans of both sides of the queue before anything reaches the backend.

06.hint: It knows which shard owns each id and reads from all of them at once.

07.hint: It drives the three partner APIs and writes down every step it took.

08.hint: It sits between the service that emits events and the group that consumes them.

09.hint: Positions flow in from the phones, nearest queries flow in from dispatch.

10.hint: The leader is chosen in one place, and the token it gets is checked in another.
